text.p: Pakistan all-rounder Aamir Sohail scored a half-century and claimed two wickets to steer his side to a comfortable four-wicket win against Australia in their limited overs World Series match on Wednesday.
Opener Sohail played the anchor role with a patient 52 as Pakistan overhauled Australia's 199 all out to reach 203 for six with 27 balls to spare at the Sydney Cricket Ground.
The left-arm orthodox spinner earlier removed all-rounder Greg Blewett for 33 and fast bowler Paul Reiffel for three as Australia laboured to master Pakistan's spin attack.
After taking two for 33 from his spell of nine overs, Sohail added 54 runs in a brisk opening partnership with Shahid Afridi.
Afridi, who joined Sohail, Mushtaq Ahmed and Saqlain Mushtaq in Pakistan's four-pronged spin attack, hammered six fours in a rapid 34 off 27 deliveries.
Ijaz Ahmed, batting at number four, lifted his side within sight of their target by hitting 58 off 83 balls before becoming one of leg-spinner Shane Warne's four victims.
The home side were dismissed in 47.1 overs after experienced all-rounder Steve Waugh gave the innings some early momentum by scoring 42 in 55 balls.
Australia suffered another blow when Reiffel was forced off the field with a hamstring strain early in the Pakistan innings.

Pakistan have summoned Ijaz Ahmed Junior and Mujahid Jamshed from home to strengthen their batting ranks after opener Saeed Anwar was ruled out for the rest of the tour because of a virus, an Australian Cricket Board spokesman said.
Australia and Pakistan lead the triangular tournament with four points, two points ahead of West Indies.
